request.prompt:
# Task
Normalize the request in `request` into a requirements specification.
- Number requirements R1, R2, ... Each needs testable acceptance criteria (concrete input -> expected outcome).
- Capture implied non-functional needs (security, reliability, observability) as their own requirements.
- Record every assumption you make.
- Ask a clarifying question (Q1, ...) for each real ambiguity. Mark it blocking only if a wrong guess would
  change the API, the data model or the security posture. Always give a sensible proposed_default.
- If human feedback answers questions, fold the answers into the requirements and assumptions and do not
  ask those questions again.
- List what is explicitly out of scope.

# Inputs

## request
# Greenfield: URL shortener service

Build a URL shortener HTTP service from scratch.

Core API
- POST /shorten takes a long URL and returns a short code and the short URL. Callers may
  supply their own custom alias instead of a generated code; aliases must be unique.
- GET /{code} redirects to the original URL. Unknown or expired codes return 404.
- GET /analytics/{code} returns click statistics for a link: total clicks, when it was
  created, and when it was last visited.
- GET /health returns service health for load balancers.

Behaviour
- Links can optionally expire after a given time.
- Reject unsafe targets: only http and https URLs, and nothing that points at localhost or
  private network addresses (SSRF protection).
- Rate-limit link creation per client so the service cannot be abused.
- Data must survive a restart.

Engineering expectations
- Clean, typed, maintainable code a new engineer can continue.
- Automated tests for every endpoint, including error cases.
- A README with setup, run and test instructions plus an API reference.


# Output format
Respond with ONE JSON object that validates against this JSON Schema. No prose and no markdown fences.

response.text:
{
  "title": "URL Shortener Service Specification",
  "problem_statement": "Design and build a secure, persistent HTTP URL shortener service that allows clients to create short links (with auto-generated codes or custom aliases), redirect to destination URLs with expiration handling, view access analytics, and enforce SSRF validation and rate limiting.",
  "requirements": [
    {
      "id": "R1",
      "text": "The service must provide an endpoint POST /shorten to create shortened URLs with optional custom alias and optional expiration time.",
      "category": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Given a valid payload `{\"url\": \"https://example.com\"}`, when POST /shorten is called, then return HTTP 201 with a generated unique `code` and the complete `short_url`.",
        "Given a valid payload `{\"url\": \"https://example.com\", \"alias\": \"my-link\"}` where 'my-link' does not exist, when POST /shorten is called, then return HTTP 201 with `code`: 'my-link'.",
        "Given a payload with an alias that already exists, when POST /shorten is called, then return HTTP 409 Conflict with an error message.",
        "Given a payload with `expires_at` in ISO 8601 format in the future, when POST /shorten is called, then store the link with the specified expiration timestamp."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R2",
      "text": "The service must provide an endpoint GET /{code} to redirect callers to the original target URL.",
      "category": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Given an active, non-expired code mapped to 'https://example.com', when GET /{code} is received, then return HTTP 302 Found (or 307) with 'Location: https://example.com'.",
        "Given a code that does not exist in the database, when GET /{code} is received, then return HTTP 404 Not Found.",
        "Given a code whose `expires_at` timestamp is earlier than current UTC time, when GET /{code} is received, then return HTTP 404 Not Found."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R3",
      "text": "The service must provide an endpoint GET /analytics/{code} returning link usage metrics and lifecycle timestamps.",
      "category": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Given an existing code that has been redirected 3 times, when GET /analytics/{code} is received, then return HTTP 200 with `total_clicks`: 3, `created_at` matching link creation time, and `last_visited_at` matching the timestamp of the last redirection.",
        "Given an existing code that has never been redirected, when GET /analytics/{code} is received, then return HTTP 200 with `total_clicks`: 0 and `last_visited_at`: null.",
        "Given a non-existent code, when GET /analytics/{code} is received, then return HTTP 404 Not Found."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R4",
      "text": "The service must provide an endpoint GET /health returning service health status for load balancers.",
      "category": "reliability",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Given the HTTP service and backing database are operational, when GET /health is requested, then return HTTP 200 OK with `{\"status\": \"healthy\"}`.",
        "Given the backing database connection is unavailable, when GET /health is requested, then return HTTP 503 Service Unavailable with `{\"status\": \"unhealthy\"}`."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R5",
      "text": "The service must validate long URLs against SSRF vulnerabilities by rejecting non-HTTP/HTTPS schemes and private/reserved/loopback network addresses.",
      "category": "security",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Given a long URL with a scheme other than http or https (e.g., 'ftp://example.com' or 'file:///etc/passwd'), when POST /shorten is called, then return HTTP 400 Bad Request.",
        "Given a long URL resolving or pointing to loopback or private IPv4/IPv6 ranges (e.g., 'http://127.0.0.1', 'http://localhost', 'http://10.0.0.1', 'http://169.254.169.254'), when POST /shorten is called, then return HTTP 400 Bad Request.",
        "Given a valid public domain resolving to a public IP address (e.g., 'https://www.google.com'), when POST /shorten is called, then allow link creation."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R6",
      "text": "The service must rate-limit link creation per client to prevent service abuse.",
      "category": "security",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Given a client IP that makes requests below the configured rate limit (e.g., 60 requests/minute), when POST /shorten is called, then all requests succeed.",
        "Given a client IP that exceeds the configured threshold within the rate limit window, when POST /shorten is called, then return HTTP 429 Too Many Requests with a 'Retry-After' header."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R7",
      "text": "The service must persist all URL records and analytics metrics across service process restarts.",
      "category": "reliability",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Given URLs and click counts stored in the system, when the HTTP service process is stopped and restarted, then GET /{code} and GET /analytics/{code} return the same data as before the restart without data loss."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R8",
      "text": "The service must provide structured logging and operational metrics for request tracing and monitoring.",
      "category": "observability",
      "priority": "should",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Given any incoming HTTP request, when processed, then emit a structured JSON log entry containing timestamp, HTTP method, path, response status code, and latency.",
        "Given an unhandled exception or database failure, when logged, then emit an error-level log entry containing the stack trace and relevant request context."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R9",
      "text": "The project must maintain automated test coverage across unit and integration levels covering all endpoints, positive paths, and error conditions.",
      "category": "reliability",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Given the test suite execution command, when run in CI or locally, then all tests pass without manual intervention and cover 200, 201, 400, 404, 409, and 429 status code scenarios across all endpoints."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "Clients are identified by client IP address (or `X-Forwarded-For` when behind a trusted reverse proxy) for the purpose of rate limiting.",
    "A standard default rate limit of 60 POST /shorten requests per minute per IP is applied unless configured otherwise.",
    "Generated codes will consist of alphanumeric characters (Base62: [a-zA-Z0-9]) with a default length of 7 characters.",
    "Custom aliases must match the regex `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{3,64}$` to prevent route collision or URL formatting issues.",
    "Data persistence is backed by a relational or document database (e.g., PostgreSQL or SQLite for local execution) surviving service restarts.",
    "Redirection uses HTTP status code 302 (Found) or 307 (Temporary Redirect) to ensure click analytics are captured on subsequent requests rather than cached permanently by browsers (HTTP 301).",
    "Analytics incrementing for GET /{code} counts every redirect request, regardless of whether it originates from unique or repeated visitors."
  ],
  "open_questions": [
    {
      "id": "Q1",
      "question": "What redirect HTTP status code should be used (e.g., 302 Found vs 307 Temporary Redirect vs 301 Moved Permanently)?",
      "why_it_matters": "Using 301 causes client/browser caching, preventing subsequent clicks from reaching the server and skewing click analytics. 302 or 307 ensures requests always hit the backend.",
      "blocking": true,
      "proposed_default": "Use HTTP 302 Found to guarantee all clicks hit the server for accurate analytics while maintaining broad client compatibility."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "question": "Should custom aliases be case-sensitive or case-insensitive?",
      "why_it_matters": "Affects the uniqueness constraints in the database, indexing strategy, and duplicate detection behavior.",
      "blocking": true,
      "proposed_default": "Case-sensitive uniqueness matching the Base62 generated codes scheme."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "question": "What is the exact rate limit threshold and window per client?",
      "why_it_matters": "Determines rate limiting data structure, memory consumption, and whether burst traffic is permitted.",
      "blocking": false,
      "proposed_default": "60 requests per minute per client IP using a sliding window or token bucket algorithm."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "question": "What storage engine is preferred for production and testing environments?",
      "why_it_matters": "Guides database driver selection, migrations, and container setup in the README.",
      "blocking": false,
      "proposed_default": "PostgreSQL for production/standard runs and SQLite for automated unit/integration test isolation."
    }
  ],
  "out_of_scope": [
    "User authentication, accounts, roles, and authorization mechanisms (API keys, JWT).",
    "Custom domain name management (vanity domains per customer).",
    "Detailed geolocation, user-agent parsing, or referrer breakdown in click analytics.",
    "Bulk URL shortening API endpoints.",
    "Web frontend / Graphical User Interface (GUI)."
  ]
}
